title: Affine case of the single-complex derived base-change criterion
statement: Let X=Spec(A), S=Spec(R), S'=Spec(R') and X'=Spec(A') be a cartesian square of affine schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-base-change], with f:X\to S and g:S'\to S, and let K correspond to a complex M^\bullet of A-modules and K' to a complex N^\bullet of A'-modules in the quasi-coherent derived categories [def-pc-derived-category]. Let L(g')^*K\to K' be a map in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{X'}), equivalently a morphism M^\bullet\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A'\to N^\bullet in D(A') via [lem-pc-affine-derived-pullback-tensor-tilde]. For a prime x' of A', let x be its image in A and let s' and s be their images in R' and R. If for every such x' and every i the canonical stalk map H^i(K_x\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_{S,s}}\mathcal O_{S',s'})\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X,x}\otimes_{\mathcal O_{S,s}}\mathcal O_{S',s'}}\mathcal O_{X',x'}\to H^i(K'_{x'}) is an isomorphism (equivalently, under the affine identifications, H^i(M^\bullet_x\otimes^L_{R_s}R'_{s'})\otimes_{A_x\otimes_{R_s}R'_{s'}}A'_{x'}\to H^i(N^\bullet_{x'})), then the induced derived pullback/direct-image comparison map [def-pc-derived-pullback, def-pc-derived-direct-image] M^\bullet\otimes^L_R R'\to M^\bullet\otimes^L_A A'\to N^\bullet is an isomorphism in D(R').

source.place: Tag 0DJ8, proof after affine reduction in Lemma single-complex-base-change-condition; Tag 0DJ9 affine case

proof.text: Write the affine cartesian square as S=Spec(R), X=Spec(A), S'=Spec(R') and X'=Spec(A') with A'=A\otimes_R R'. Under the affine quasi-coherent derived equivalence, K and K' correspond to complexes M^\bullet of A-modules and N^\bullet of A'-modules, and the derived direct images and pullbacks in the comparison map correspond to derived module tensors. Thus the comparison is represented by the composite M^\bullet\otimes_R^\mathbf L R'\to M^\bullet\otimes_A^\mathbf L A'\to N^\bullet in D(R').

source.place: Tag 0DJ8, proof after affine reduction: affine identifications and the displayed module comparison

proof.text: The given morphism L(g')^*K\to K' corresponds to a morphism M^\bullet\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A'\to N^\bullet in D(A'), so its maps on cohomology are A'-linear. Composing it with the comparison morphism c:M^\bullet\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R'\to M^\bullet\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A' [lem-pc-affine-derived-base-change-comparison-map], whose cohomology maps H^i(c) are A'-linear by that statement, and taking cohomology gives an A'-linear map H^i(M^\bullet\otimes_R^\mathbf L R')\to H^i(N^\bullet) for every i.

source.place: Tag 0DJ8 affine proof: 'Equivalently, it is that for all i ...'

proof.text: At a compatible prime x'=\mathfrak q' of A', with images x=\mathfrak q of A and s'=\mathfrak p' of R', s=\mathfrak p of R, localize the A'-linear map of Step 2 at \mathfrak q' (apply -\otimes_{A'}A'_{\mathfrak q'}). For the first arrow, the localization identities and compatibility of [lem-pc-affine-derived-base-change-comparison-map] identify H^i(c)\otimes_{A'}A'_{\mathfrak q'} with H^i(M^\bullet_{\mathfrak q}\otimes^\mathbf L_{R_{\mathfrak p}}R'_{\mathfrak p'})\otimes_{A_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_{R_{\mathfrak p}}R'_{\mathfrak p'}}A'_{\mathfrak q'}\to H^i(M^\bullet_{\mathfrak q}\otimes^\mathbf L_{A_{\mathfrak q}}A'_{\mathfrak q'}); no model of M^\bullet\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R' as a complex of A'-modules is used. For the second arrow, both P^\bullet\otimes_A A' (the model of that statement) and N^\bullet are complexes of A'-modules, and localization at A'\setminus\mathfrak q' is exact [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact], so it commutes with kernels and images of differentials and preserves quasi-isomorphisms; hence H^i(C)_{\mathfrak q'}\cong H^i(C_{\mathfrak q'}) for C=P^\bullet\otimes_A A',N^\bullet, and the localized second arrow is H^i of the localization M^\bullet_{\mathfrak q}\otimes^\mathbf L_{A_{\mathfrak q}}A'_{\mathfrak q'}\to N^\bullet_{\mathfrak q'} of the given morphism. Under the affine identifications of stalks with localizations [lem-weil-pbc-spec-tilde-stalk-localization] and of derived pullback with derived tensor [lem-pc-affine-derived-pullback-tensor-tilde], K_x=M^\bullet_{\mathfrak q}, K'_{x'}=N^\bullet_{\mathfrak q'}, \mathcal O_{S,s}=R_{\mathfrak p}, \mathcal O_{S',s'}=R'_{\mathfrak p'}, \mathcal O_{X,x}=A_{\mathfrak q}, \mathcal O_{X',x'}=A'_{\mathfrak q'}, so the localized map is the canonical stalk map of the hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0DJ8 affine proof: localization identity immediately before 'we see that these two conditions are equivalent'

proof.text: The stalk hypothesis therefore says that the map H^i(M^\bullet\otimes_R^\mathbf L R')\to H^i(N^\bullet) is bijective after localization at every maximal ideal of A' (maximal ideals are primes and are included among the compatible primes). By the module localization criterion [lem-weil-pbc-linear-map-bijective-at-maximal-localizations], this cohomology map is bijective for every i. Hence the displayed map of complexes is a quasi-isomorphism, so the comparison morphism in D(R') is an isomorphism.
